key_insight: Se/ZnMgO photodiodes act as self-powered visual synapses whose weight can be potentiated or depressed purely by light wavelength, with photon energy determining the update direction.
engineering_relevance: This enables zero-bias optoelectronic memory and in-sensor computing for low-power vision hardware, with direct relevance to flexible neuromorphic devices.
method: Used Se/ZnMgO thin-film photodiodes operated at zero bias to map photocurrent changes to synaptic weight updates.
Compared wavelength-dependent responses under 365 nm and 455 nm illumination, including flux-dependent potentiation/depression and multi-level learning behavior.
Combined optical simulations and drift-diffusion modeling to link the switching mechanism to interface defect occupation.
evidence_signal: At equal photon flux, 365 nm pulses increased photocurrent by 38% while 455 nm pulses decreased it, with up to 19 distinguishable levels per branch; a digit-recognition network reached 89% accuracy without noise and 85% with measured noise.
watch_item: Performance depends on defect-mediated interface states, so reproducibility, environmental stability, and large-scale fabrication control may be challenging.
paper_title: Wavelength-selective bidirectional plasticity in self-powered Se/ZnMgO visual synapses
